audit.whatIsWrong: content win[1] through win[5] read Skill, Skill, Skill, Sylas, Skill, but whys[1] says you start punishing his walk-ups at 2, whys[2] says your Q pattern punishes him off his E cooldown, whys[3] says your drain out-heals his W sustain, whys[4] says your R heal amp wins the brawl at 6, and whys[5] says your first-item spike out-brawls him. The packet chart reads Aatrox through First item.
audit.why: Both of Sylas's escapes are dashes, and Infernal Chains grounds. Once Aatrox has W he removes Sylas's entire disengage, which is why 50.73% over 5977 games sits with Aatrox in lane and only flips at full build.
audit.corrected: Levels 2 through First item all read Aatrox; Two+ items stays Sylas.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hijack is discussed at Level 6 and late without ever giving its cooldown, and none of Sylas's basic abilities carry numbers.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30 — by rank 3 he re-steals an ultimate every 30 seconds, so 'hold your R so he can't copy a fresh one' is a much shorter-lived plan than the entry implies. Chain Lash is 10s, Kingslayer 12s down to 6s, Abscond/Abduct 13s down to 9s.
audit.corrected: 80s rank-1 and 30s rank-3 Hijack stated in spikes[1]; Kingslayer and Abscond cooldowns stated in mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry only ever says 'dodge his E2 pull' and never states what Infernal Chains actually does to him. Both of Sylas's mobility tools are dashes — Kingslayer is a lunge, Abscond/Abduct a dash with a chain recast — and Infernal Chains drags anyone who does not clear the impact area back to its centre. That forces him to spend a dash purely to escape the zone, and a Sylas who has spent Abscond has no way out of the follow-up.
audit.why: Riot's text: Infernal Chains — 'Aatrox smashes the ground, dealing damage to the first enemy hit. Champions and large monsters have to leave the impact area quickly or they will be dragged to the center'; Kingslayer — 'Sylas lunges at an enemy'; Abscond/Abduct — 'Sylas dashes to a location.' The sequencing that matters is chain-on-his-step-up: he either eats the drag back into your Q pattern, or burns his 13s escape to leave the zone and then has nothing when you commit.
audit.corrected: Infernal Chains framed as the tool that forces his escape dash out early; hold it for his step-up, not the wave.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says 'your drain out-heals his W sustain' but never says how to make that true.
audit.why: Kingslayer heals him on every champion hit, so his sustain scales with how long the fight runs. Grievous Wounds is what makes the extended trade the entry recommends actually favour you.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal named in the full-layer tldr.

edits.before: Your window opens: sidestep his E2 chain-pull and land Q3 sweetspot into your own W — his short-range poke can't out-trade your drain when his E is down.
edits.after: Your window: chain the ground he steps onto — Infernal Chains drags him back to its centre unless he burns Abscond. Either way his escape is gone when Q3 lands.

edits.before: Even with R theft on the table, your World Ender heal-amp out-brawls him — just bait or hold your ult so he can't copy a fresh one, then drain-trade him down on his E cooldown.
edits.after: Even with Hijack on the table your World Ender heal amp out-brawls him — hold your ult so he cannot copy a fresh one, but at rank 3 he re-steals every 30s. Chain him and drain.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay yours. With two points in Q you can sidestep his E2 chain-pull and answer with a Q3 sweetspot into W Infernal Chains, and your drain out-heals his W sustain in an extended trade. Force these whenever his E is down — that's his only escape and reposition tool. At 6 his R can steal your World Ender, so bait or hold your ult; do that and your heal amp still wins the brawl rather than handing him a fresh ultimate to copy.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay yours. Save Infernal Chains for his step-up, never the wave: leave the zone late and it drags him back to the centre, so he must spend Abscond (13s) just to get out, and Kingslayer (12s) is a lunge toward you, not away. Q3 sweetspot into that and drain — Kingslayer heals him on every champion hit, so Grievous Wounds decides the long trade. At 6 hold your ult against Hijack, but rank 3 refreshes it every 30s.

edits.before: Dodge his E2 pull so he can't reposition for Q/W
edits.after: Chain his step-up so he must burn Abscond first

edits.before: Sylas changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Sylas E chain, W heal, and stolen Aatrox R. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Sylas wants to enter inside Aatrox clean Q hits on the outer edge (where it hurts most), force melee trades, and punish Aatrox after Q/E are down.
edits.after: Sylas changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Kingslayer's heal on every champion hit and a Hijack that copies World Ender every 30s at rank 3. Aatrox wins by holding Infernal Chains for the step-up — leave its zone late and Sylas is dragged back to the centre, so he must spend his 13s Abscond to escape — then spacing with the first two Darkin Blade swings and buying Grievous Wounds early.

edits.before: Sylas E chain, W heal, and stolen Aatrox R
edits.after: Chains drag him; Abscond is his only out

notes: Petricite Burst (Sylas's passive) is never named anywhere in the entry — after each spell his next basic attack whirls his chains for bonus magic damage, which is where his poke comes from. No length-safe slot to add it. IMPORTANT: champ-data/_kits/_missing/aatrox.json claims 'Your Infernal Chains (W) shuts off Sylas's Kingslayer (W), Abscond/Abduct (E)' on a grounding flag. Riot's own W description says nothing about grounding — it drags targets who linger back to the centre. I did NOT write the grounding claim; the generator rule behind it is producing the same false statement for Urgot and Zaahen in this champion's missing file too.
